we have measured the longest spin echo times for a single-electron spin qubit to date, and we have developed a semi-classical theory that quantitatively explains the measured spin echo behavior.
the coherence time of electron spins can be extended to 200 $\mu s$ by using a multiple-pulse spin-echo sequence.
we have demonstrated long coherence of electron spins in gate defined quantum dots, and have identified and quantitatively accounted the nuclear spin bath as the primary source of this decoherence.

the development of quantum computing devices based on the electron spin.
the development of a new type of quantum bit (qubit) based on a single spin in a semiconductor quantum dot, and the demonstration of long-lived spin coherence times of up to 200 $\mu s$.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have shown how to extend the electron spin coherence times of GaAs quantum dots to the microsecond range, and that this is due to the interplay of the electron-nuclear spin coupling and the magnetic field.
the coherence of a single electron spin in a semiconductor quantum dot can be extended to 200 $\mu s$ by using a combination of a magnetic field of a few hundred mT and a multiple-pulse spin echo.
nuclear spin bath induced decoherence is not an obstacle for quantum computation in semiconductor quantum dots, but that it can be controlled.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that nuclear spins are not a showstopper for spin qubits, and that we have demonstrated a way to overcome their detrimental effects.

the coherence times of the electron spin qubits in gate defined Gaas quantum dots are not limited by the interaction with nuclear spins, but rather by the electron spin relaxation time, which is about 1 $\mathrm{\mu}$s at low magnetic fields.
the coherence time in GaAs quantum dots is not limited by the nuclear spin bath.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coherence time of electron spin qubit in a GaAs quantum dot can be extended by two orders of magnitudes by applying a multiple-pulse spin echo sequence, and the decoherence is mainly caused by the interaction between electron spin qubit and nuclear spins in the host lattice.
, in the absence of nuclear spin diffusion and with proper control of the nuclear spin bath, the coherence of electron spin qubit can be extended to the microsecond timescale, and even longer.
nuclear spin bath is not the limiting factor in quantum computing with electron spins in GaAs quantum dots.
